worked.problem: The quadratic sequence begins 17, 25, 37, 53, 73, … . At which positive integer position does the value 157 occur? Show that your position is valid.
actions: Write T₁ to T₅: 17, 25, 37, 53, 73. Their first differences are 8, 12, 16, 20.
Second differences are 4, 4, 4, so a = 4/2 = 2.
Use T₂ − T₁ = 3a + b = 8 to obtain b = 2; then T₁ = a + b + c = 17 gives c = 13. Thus Tₙ = 2n² + 2n + 13.
Rearrange 2n² + (2)n + (13) = 157: (n − 8)(2n + 18) = 0. Thus n = 8 or n = −18/2; reject the negative position.
Answer: n = 8. For n ≥ 1, consecutive increments are positive; T₍7₎ = 125 < 157, so this is the only positive position.
worked.check: Answer: n = 8. For n ≥ 1, consecutive increments are positive; T₍7₎ = 125 < 157, so this is the only positive position.
